rag_hits.title: Flood Resilience at NYCHA — Lessons Learned
rag_hits.text: Letter from the Vice President for Recovery & Resilience Dear New Yorkers, Hurricane Sandy devasted New York City in October 2012. Despite living in a city with 520 miles of coastline, residents had never grappled with storm surge at this scale. Salt water and debris covered huge swaths of the five boroughs, including many NYCHA campuses. Unlike prior major storms, the impacts didn’t dissipate when the weather improved. Salt water corroded critical infrastructure that was stored below grade. The homes of tens of thousands of public housing residents—most of whom couldn’t evacuate before the storm—were without water, power, heat, hot water, or elevator service for weeks.

final.paragraph:
This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and baked data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**Hazard Reader.**
This address sits outside the empirical 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation footprint (NYC OEM) [sandy_inundation]. This address sits in FEMA flood zone X, per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970203F, effective 2007 [fema_nfhl]. No Hurricane Ida (Sept 2021) high-water marks were surveyed within 800 m of this address [ida_hwm]. Nearest USGS-surveyed mark: South of Bedford Ave., between north 12th St. and Lorimer Ave., in McCarren Park, Brooklyn (2396 m away) [ida_hwm]. Experimental: satellite-detected surface water about 14 hours after Hurricane Ida (Sentinel-2, 2021-09-02): 0 water polygons within 500 m of this address, nearest 8722.4 m away [prithvi_water]. Most are marsh, shoreline and park water; street and basement flooding had drained by then and is not visible in this layer. Elevation 6.51 m; this point sits at the 66.2th percentile of elevation within a 200 m window (lower percentile = topographic low); HAND 6.51 m above nearest drainage; TWI 8.03 [microtopo]. Local basin relief: 4.92 m [microtopo]. Experimental: Policy passages retrieved from the NYC flood-policy corpus for this place: 1 (embedding retrieval; entity tags are experimental) [policy_corpus].

**Live Observer.**
2 FloodNet community sensor(s) within 600 m have logged 6 above-curb flood event(s) in the last 3 years [floodnet]. Peak depth recorded by these sensors: 96 mm [floodnet]. 17 NYC 311 flood-related complaints filed within 200 m of this location in the last 5 years [nyc311]. Most common descriptor: Catch Basin Clogged/Flooding (Use Comments) (SC). Latest METAR at Central Park, NY (7.3 km away): 16.1°C (obs 2026-09-26T18:51) [nws_obs]. Latest reading at The Battery, NY: 2.83 ft above MLLW (+2.35 ft vs predicted tide), observed 2026-09-26 16:00 [noaa_tides].

**Asset Register.**
2 MTA subway entrances within 800 m of this address: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 2 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [mta_entrance_exposure]. 5 NYCHA developments within 2000 m of this address: 3 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 2 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [nycha_development_exposure]. 4 NYC DOE schools within 1500 m of this address: 4 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 0 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doe_school_exposure]. 5 hospitals within 3000 m of this address: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 2 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doh_hospital_exposure].

**Projector.**
2 active NWS alerts at this point: Coastal Flood Warning (Severe), Coastal Flood Advisory (Minor) [nws_alerts]. Experimental: a TTM model fine-tuned on Battery gauge history, with no wind or pressure input, forecasts a peak surge residual of 0.59 m at The Battery about 1 h ahead [ttm_battery_surge]. Use NOAA ETSS or the Stevens Flood Advisory System for storm decisions. Experimental: 2 flood-related 311 complaints within 200 m over the last 512 days; a zero-shot TTM forecast with no rainfall input and no backtest projects about 0.02 per week for the next 96 days [ttm_311_forecast]. NPCC4 (2024) projects sea-level rise at the Battery of 0.38 m (15 in) by the 2050s and 0.79 m (31 in) by 2100 at the median, relative to 2000-2004; 90th percentile 0.74 m and 1.65 m [npcc4_slr].

**Out of scope.** This briefing does not assess title, structural condition, or compliance with specific zoning rules. Where a probe was offline at run time, the relevant section omits that signal.
